item.title: Ants build living bridges by following one local rule: stop when someone walks over you
item.description: Army ants form bridges out of their own bodies to shorten their path across gaps. Researchers found that each ant follows a simple rule: if it feels traffic passing over it, it freezes in place; when traffic drops, it leaves. The bridge grows and shrinks without any ant knowing the overall shape, trading workers for shorter travel time.

item.title: How fungal networks decide which tree gets the nutrients
item.description: Underground fungal threads connect trees across a forest. A new study suggests the network routes more carbon toward connections that are used more often, and lets unused threads wither, a pattern similar to self-organizing transport networks.

item.title: Octopus arms make decisions without asking the brain
item.description: Two thirds of an octopus's neurons sit in its arms. Experiments show each arm can explore and grab food using local sensing, reporting to the central brain only occasionally. The animal trades central control for fast parallel exploration.
